summary: As of November 13, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.23 percentage points, -0.19 percentage points over five trading days, and the junk-versus-safe gap is 2.34 percentage points. VIX is 19.30 and the 3-month VIX is 20.62, so near-term fear is below the 3-month reading. The Nasdaq-100 is -10.5 percent from its trailing high, semiconductors are -7.1 percent versus their 200-day average, and 73 percent of the 30-name list is above its own 200-day average.
what_would_change_this: The headline would leave risk-on if junk spreads reached 4.50 percentage points, near-term volatility rose above the 3-month reading by more than half a point, or the Nasdaq-100 fell more than 10 percent below its trailing high.
what_the_tape_is_saying: As of November 13, 2026, junk-bond spreads are 3.23 percentage points and are down 0.19 percentage points over five trading days. Investment-grade spreads are down 0.04 percentage points over those same five trading days. The CCC-minus-BB gap is 11.30 percentage points. Of the 0.14 percentage-point move in the all-in junk yield, 0.19 was the credit spread and 0.33 was Treasury rates. The 10-year yield is 5.15 percent as of November 13, 2026 and the 30-year is 5.47 percent as of November 13, 2026, a gap of 0.32 percentage points. Brent is 91.65 dollars a barrel as of November 17, 2026 (+0.17 percent over five trading days), and the curve is an unpublished curve shape. The 5-year inflation breakeven is 2.25 percent as of November 16, 2026, down 0.04 percentage points over five observations. The 10-year real yield is 2.91 percent as of November 13, 2026. The broad dollar index is 122.65 as of November 13, 2026, +1.08 index points over 20 observations. VIX is 19.30 as of November 13, 2026.
